name: 07-adaptive-coevolution
title: Adaptive coevolution (opinions + rewiring)
question: When topology and node state co-adapt, does the network organise into like-minded communities?
hypothesis: Letting nodes rewire away from differing neighbours and toward similar ones (while opinions also spread) raises assortativity and segregates the two opinions — the coevolution bridge between Family A and dynamics-on-networks.
objective: Run the adaptive_rewire reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `adaptive_rewire` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

config.title: Adaptive coevolution (opinions + rewiring)

expected_behavior.name: ad-conserves-structure
expected_behavior.condition: node and edge counts are conserved (rewiring + state flips, no growth)
expected_behavior.rationale: Each step either flips one opinion or moves one edge endpoint.

expected_behavior.name: ad-segregates
expected_behavior.condition: the network reorganises toward like-minded ties
expected_behavior.rationale: Rewiring toward same-state nodes raises opinion assortativity.

behavior_tests.name: ad-edge-count-conserved
behavior_tests.description: Edge count is conserved (rewiring, not growth).

findings.name: adaptive_rewire-signature
findings.summary: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.
findings.detail: Node and edge counts stay fixed while the blue/orange opinions segregate into like-minded neighbourhoods — the coevolutionary self-organisation Gross & Blasius review, and the natural bridge to dynamics-on-networks (Family B).

report.verdict: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

followup_proposals.title: SBML reactors on a state-driven adaptive network
followup_proposals.motivation: Here the rewiring is driven by a DISCRETE opinion; Family C rewired by a fixed rule. The richer case lets a CONTINUOUS node state (an SBML readout) drive the rewiring — closing the state→topology feedback.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Rewire edges based on a per-node SBML observable (e.g. oscillator phase or a protein level), so topology self-organises around the continuous dynamics.
